content_of_post_to_comment:
i’m 22 diagnosed with anxiety, bpd, depression and adhd and find myself getting really worked up and angry quite quickly making me build resentments or start finding smaller issues much more infuriating.

i’m at university and have been living with my bestfriends for multiple years but decided to branch out and live with new/different people to make my relationships with my friends better as well as to try new things.

i really want to get along with these new people in the house i’m in now - its only been a couple months, so i’m trying to stay positive

but there are issues i have like leaving the toilet seat up (which i’ve really politely asked about a few times), the front door being left completely wide open, slamming doors and talking really loudly through the house at 3am. which i have all calmly and nicely brought up. but i’m beginning to feel a bit crazy and don’t know if it’s me being uptight or if it’s somewhat reasonable. everyone else in the house doesn’t seem fazed so i don’t want to make a big deal or try and cause any conflict, but i start getting quite irritated by these situations.

edit/context:
i have been in and out of therapy since i was 12 and am on antidepressants, i have done a lot of working on myself, especially with my patience
but it’s getting to be a lot and i need advice on how to remain patient and calm with the people i’m living with as to not cause issues
🙏❤️
comment: I think there’s a difference between being “uptight” and needing basic consideration in a shared house. The door being left wide open and people making noise at 3am aren’t just preferences, they affect everyone. At the same time, when you notice yourself spiraling, it might help to ask “is this a house rule issue or a stress trigger?” before deciding how much energy to give it.
